format: RFC 6902 JSON Patch; paths relative to the target document

patch.value: This assumes * is a matrix product. In NumPy * is element-wise, so it keeps shape (2, 3).
Neither operator gives (2, 2) here. * is element-wise, so A * B.T keeps the common shape (2, 3); and if * were a matrix product, (2x3)(2x3) would not even be defined.
A * B.T is valid because both arrays have shape (2, 3). A * B (without .T) would fail to broadcast.

This is what you would predict if * were the matrix product: (2x3)(2x3) has inner dimensions 3 and 2. But * is element-wise, and A and B.T both have shape (2, 3), so it runs. (A * B, without .T, would fail to broadcast.)

value.rationale: Predicting (2, 2) for A * B.T treats the element-wise * as the matrix product, the converse confusion of MC-004 (element-wise vs matrix product).
Predicting a ValueError for A * B.T follows from reading the element-wise * as the matrix product (the converse confusion of MC-004): a (2x3)(2x3) matrix product is undefined.
